1. 
Introduction/Context 
 
Workplace health and wellbeing of employees are intrinsically important to people led 
organisations such as Technological Universities. Ireland’s new Technological Universities are 
committed to promoting healthy workplaces and to working towards the best possible 
working environment for the wellbeing of their employees. One of the key challenges for the 
TUs will be the management of geographically dispersed campuses to provide the best 
education for its students. It is also recognised that these geographically dispersed campuses 
will provide opportunities for employees to seek to move location for personal, professional, 
or other reasons. To this end, it has been agreed that the development of a policy for the 
voluntary transfer of employees is both welcome and necessary. While recognising the 
desirability of facilitating any individual member of staff’s wishes relating to transferring 
between campuses it is accepted that the academic and business needs of the TU must be 
given priority, including existing industrial relations agreements. 
 
2. 
Purpose 
 
The purpose of this policy is to set out clear and equitable principles and policy that provide 
for the voluntary transfer of employees within South East Technological University (SETU), 
supporting both staff wellbeing and operational needs. 
 
3. 
Scope 
 
This agreement sets out the principles for the voluntary transfer of employees from one 
unit/function on a base or location/place of work to another, or from one campus to a different 
campus in SETU. 
It shall be made generally available and published publicly via the SETU website. 
 
4. 
Principles 
 
The general principles which should be followed:

5 
 
4.1 
It is management’s ultimate responsibility to decide on the allocation of employees 
and the disposition of resources within the Technological University in the context of 
academic and business needs. 
4.2 
All procedures and decisions are to be conducted in a transparent and equitable 
manner. It is expected that an employee seeking a voluntary transfer will set out the reasons 
for the transfer in writing and these will be treated in confidence by the HR Division of the 
university 
4.3 
Applications for transfer will be considered in a positive manner and all reasonable efforts 
to accommodate requests will be made. 
 
4.4 
The voluntary nature of this process will remain paramount at all times. 
 
 
5. Definitions 
 
For the purpose of this policy, a voluntary campus transfer is defined as a move initiated by 
an employee from one unit/function on a base or location/place of work to another or from 
one campus to a different campus in South East Technological University, either for personal, 
professional, or other reasons, and not arising from a management-initiated redeployment. 
 
6. 
Policy 
 
SETU recognises that voluntary campus transfers can support employee well-being, personal 
circumstances, and organisational effectiveness. It is not necessary that a vacancy or 
requirement for the skill set of the applicant in their proposed new campus/function/unit 
must always exist, though normally it would be the case that an applicant would move into a 
vacant post, where one exists following application of any industrial relations agreements. 
Where an application is made on humanitarian grounds and/or for urgent personal reasons, 
management will explore appropriate creative solutions within the constraints of academic 
and business requirements. 
 
Applications can be made at any time, but the timing of any transfers will be subject to 
academic and business needs and will require consultation with all relevant parties. Academic 
applications should be made by end of April for consideration for transfer for the following 
academic year (if possible). Consequently, it is expected that most such academic transfers 
will occur at the beginning of an academic year. 
 
Staff must hold a Permanent position or have acquired a Contract of Indefinite Duration

6 
 
(CID) to apply for a transfer. They must have successfully completed their probationary period 
and must have at least 1 years of service inclusive of their probationary period. Applicants 
must also possess the relevant qualifications for the post. 
 
Discussions regarding personal development between the employee and both the current and 
prospective academic units may be included as part of the process in accordance with GDPR 
requirements. 
 
Applications for transfer will remain on file and open for consideration until withdrawn by an 
employee or they have accepted an offer of a voluntary campus transfer or have refused two 
offers of a voluntary campus transfer. 
 
Staff members who decline two offers of transfer will not be considered for another transfer 
until the expiration of twelve months from the date of last refusal. In this case, after the twelve 
months have expired staff members must complete a new application. 
 
If a staff member has been successful in a transfer, one cannot seek to be considered for 
another transfer for 12 months after the start date of the transfer role. 
 
The operation of this policy shall have regard to other agreements in relation to temporary 
employees and the augmentation of hours. 
 
Any employee unhappy with the operation of this policy will be able to avail of the Grievance 
Procedure of the Technological University as is normal. 
 
7. 
Responsibility and Authority 
 
The HR /Recruitment department will co-ordinate all transfer requests however all final 
decisions regarding transfers rest with the relevant SETU Hiring Manager, who will balance 
employee requests with the academic and business requirements of the Technological 
University.

9. 
Guidance 
 
The Human Resources Department will provide guidance to staff on the process for 
submitting transfer requests. 
Information & guidance is also available from the Technological University’s HR Policies page 
on the website. https://www.setu.ie/staff/hr-policies 
 
10. Compliance 
 
It is expected that all employees of SETU will comply with this policy. 
 
11. Useful Links

12. Review of Policy 
 
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date and/or as soon as possible following 
new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
 
13. Policy Author 
 
The authors of this policy are the HR Managers. Any feedback or issues arising on 
implementation of this policy should be communicated to the policy authors. They are 
responsible to ensure that the Policy Owner is aware of these comments when reviewing 
the policy.
